statement: One federal body has exclusive power over advertising and marketing communication in Nigeria.
instrument: Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria Act, 2022 (Act No. 23)
prevents: Telling an owner that platform rules are the only rules that apply to their posts.
detail: ARCON is established with "exclusive power to determine, pronounce upon, administer, monitor and enforce compliance by persons and organisations on matters relating to advertisements, advertising, and marketing communication in Nigeria".

statement: Advertising aimed at the Nigerian market must be legal, decent, honest and truthful.
instrument: Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria Act, 2022 (Act No. 23)
prevents: Writing a superlative or urgency line that is not true, or implying a claim is just "marketing talk".
detail: A core objective is to "ensure that all advertisement exposed and directed at the Nigerian market is legal, decent, honest, truthful, respectful, and mindful of the Nigerian culture ... devoid of misinformation or disinformation".

statement: A standards panel reviews advertisements against the law and the advertising code of ethics.
instrument: Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria Act, 2022 (Act No. 23)
prevents: Presenting a self-declared "compliance check" as if it were the regulator's approval.
caveat: The Act creates the panel and the offence. The pre-exposure clearance procedure itself sits in the Nigerian Code of Advertising Practice and ARCON vetting guidelines, which were not retrieved as primary text for this register — see NG-ARCON-06.
detail: The Advertising Standards Panel (ASP) "is charged with the responsibility of ensuring that advertising and all advertisements conform with the prevailing laws of the Federation and the code of ethics of the advertising profession".

statement: Exposing an advertisement that breaches the Act is an offence, with statutory minimum fines.
instrument: Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria Act, 2022 (Act No. 23)
prevents: Assuming a post is "just content", not an advertisement, and therefore outside any penalty.
caveat: Statutory minima, not the amounts actually imposed in any particular case. Do not quote a fine figure as though it were a current enforcement tariff.
detail: A person or organisation that "exposes any advertisement that contravene any provision of this Act, commits an offence"; on conviction an individual faces "a fine of at least N500,000 or imprisonment for a term of one year or both" and an organisation "a fine of at least N1,000,000".

statement: Directors and managers can be personally caught when a company breaches the advertising Act.
instrument: Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria Act, 2022 (Act No. 23)
prevents: Treating compliance as one junior person's job with no owner sign-off.
detail: Where an offence by a body corporate "is proved to have been committed with the connivance of or to be attributable to any neglect on the part of any director, manager, secretary or other similar officer", that officer is deemed guilty and punished accordingly.

statement: Vetting submissions are normally made through a registered practitioner, with the actual creative.
instrument: ARCON vetting procedure as summarised by Nigerian legal-practice commentary
prevents: Assuming a client can submit vetting themselves, or that a URL is an acceptable submission.
caveat: Read from commentary, not from ARCON's own guidelines. Confirm current forms, fees and exemptions directly with ARCON before advising a client.
detail: Reported procedure: formal application to the Director-General, Standards Panel Form 001 signed by a registered practitioner (Associate Member or above), advertiser authorisation letter, the actual advert material (links generally not accepted), and sector approvals such as NAFDAC where relevant.

statement: Digital and social advertising has been brought into vetting, with enforcement reported on social platforms.
instrument: ARCON digital vetting enforcement as reported in Nigerian business and legal press
prevents: Stating as fact that "every Instagram post now needs ARCON approval" (or the reverse) without checking.
caveat: This is the single most consequential and least settled item in this register. Outlets disagree on scope, amounts and court outcomes; the BusinessDay piece is partly paywalled. Treat as an open question for the owner/legal adviser, not a quotable fact.
detail: Trade and legal commentary report a 2025 ARCON position that digital adverts must be vetted and approved before exposure, and enforcement notices to small online vendors. Enforcement scale and the litigation position are reported inconsistently across outlets.

statement: Marketing representations must not be false, incorrect, misleading or deceptive.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: A vague but flattering claim ("we clean everywhere", "space for anything") that a buyer relies on.
detail: A supplier must not make a representation "in a manner that is likely to imply any false or incorrect representation", "that is reasonably misleading or likely to be misleading in any material respect", or "erroneous, fraudulent or deceptive" — including as to the nature, properties, advantages or uses of the service, the conditions of supply, and the price.

statement: Performance and efficacy claims need an adequate and proper test, and the seller carries the proof.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: "This doubled our enquiries" / "works every time" with no test behind it.
caveat: The section speaks of "products"; read it as applying to services with local advice. Do not cite the section number to a client as settled law without a lawyer.
detail: No representation "in the form of a statement, warranty or guarantee of performance, efficacy or length of life of products that is not based on an adequate and proper test ... the proof of which lies on the person making the representation".

statement: A misleading representation about a material fact creates liability for damages and restitution.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: Leaving an old price, coverage area or turnaround promise online because "people ask anyway".
detail: Where a supplier "directly or indirectly expresses or implies a false, misleading or deceptive representation concerning a material fact", or "fails to correct an apparent misapprehension", the undertaking "is liable for damages to any person damaged, and shall be ordered to make monetary restitution".

statement: You may not imply sponsorship, approval or affiliation you do not have.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: A badge, "as featured in", partner logo, or "certified" claim that has no paperwork behind it.
detail: A person acting for a supplier shall not "falsely represent that the person has any sponsorship, approval or affiliation".

statement: A published testimonial needs the person's actual words and their written permission.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: Writing a plausible-sounding customer quote, or lightly editing one for a slide.
caveat: Permission must be in writing and the wording must match what was approved.
detail: A supplier may not publish a testimonial unless it can establish that it "was previously made or published by the person by whom the test was made or the testimonial was given", or that before publication "it was approved and permission to make or publish it was given in writing".

statement: Consumer-facing notices and information must be in plain, understandable language.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: Burying cover conditions or turnaround terms in jargon and fine print.
detail: Information must be "in plain language" if no form is prescribed — the test being whether an ordinary consumer with "average literacy skills and minimal experience" could understand "without undue effort".

statement: A displayed price is binding, and the lowest displayed price wins.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: Posting "from ₦X" then quoting higher, or leaving two conflicting prices live.
detail: A supplier "shall not require a consumer to pay a price for any goods or services higher than the displayed price", and where more than one price is displayed, not higher than "the lower or lowest of the prices so displayed".

statement: Terms that strip a consumer's statutory rights are void.
instrument: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act, 2018
prevents: Copying a "no refunds" policy line into a service caption.
detail: "All sales final", blanket no-refund and similar terms are void to the extent they waive or deprive a consumer of a right set out in the Act.

statement: The consumer regulator actively inspects markets for description and quantity mismatches.
instrument: FCCPC enforcement releases
prevents: Treating an inaccurate product description as a private customer-service matter.
caveat: Use as evidence that enforcement happens in practice. It is not a prediction about any specific business or sector.
detail: The Commission has publicly reported enforcement against traders selling goods that did not match their declared descriptions and quantities, citing ss.123 and 125 of the FCCPA.

statement: Personal data must be processed fairly, for stated purposes, and kept to the minimum needed.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: A booking form that asks for a phone number, address and ID "in case we need it".
detail: Principles require processing that is "fair, lawful and transparent"; collected "for specified, explicit, and legitimate purposes"; "adequate, relevant, and limited to the minimum necessary"; kept no longer than necessary; accurate; and secure.

statement: There must be a lawful basis for processing — consent is only one of them.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: Assuming every data question is solved by adding a consent checkbox.
detail: Processing is lawful where the data subject consented, or where necessary for a contract, a legal obligation, vital interests, a public-interest task, or legitimate interests that do not override the person's rights.

statement: Consent must be affirmative; silence or a pre-ticked box is not consent.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: Pre-ticked "I agree to receive offers" boxes, or counting a form submission as marketing consent.
detail: The controller "shall bear the burden of proof" for consent; "silence or inactivity ... shall not constitute consent"; consent "shall be in the affirmative, and not based on a pre-selected confirmation".

statement: People must be told what you do with their data, in a privacy notice they can actually read.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: Collecting WhatsApp enquiries with no stated purpose, retention or contact route.
detail: Before collecting data the controller must give its identity and contact, the lawful basis and purposes, recipients, the person's rights, the retention period, the right to complain to the Commission, and any automated decision-making — "in a privacy policy and expressed in clear, concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible format".

statement: People can ask for a copy, correction, erasure or a pause on their data.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: Having no route to answer "please delete my details" beyond asking the owner to remember.
detail: Rights include confirmation and purposes of processing, "a copy of data subject's personal data in a commonly used electronic format", correction or deletion of inaccurate data, erasure "without undue delay", and restriction of processing.

statement: Withdrawing consent must be as easy as giving it, and opting out of marketing must be honoured.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: A broadcast list with no opt-out that anyone can actually use.
detail: A data subject "shall have the right to withdraw, at any time, consent"; the controller "shall ensure that it is as easy for the data subject to withdraw, as to give consent"; and where someone objects to direct marketing, "the personal data shall no longer be processed for such purposes".

statement: People can refuse decisions made purely by an algorithm, and can demand a human look.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: An auto-reply that declines, prices, or rejects an enquiry with no human route.
caveat: Applies to decisions with legal or similarly significant effects. A simple auto-acknowledgement is not the same thing — do not overstate this as "all automation needs human review".
detail: A data subject has "the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing of personal data, including profiling, which produces legal or similar significant effects", with rights to "obtain human intervention", express a view, and contest the decision.

statement: A personal data breach must be reported to the Commission within 72 hours.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: A leaked customer list with no plan and no notification route.
detail: A controller shall, "within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach which is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of individuals, notify the Commission", and must tell affected people where the risk is high.

statement: Sending personal data outside Nigeria needs a documented legal basis.
instrument: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act No. 37)
prevents: Pasting customer details into whichever overseas tool is convenient, with no record of why it is allowed.
detail: Transfer from Nigeria is not permitted unless the recipient is subject to a law, binding corporate rules, contractual clauses, code or certification affording adequate protection, or another condition applies — and the basis and adequacy must be recorded.

statement: Registration as a "controller of major importance" can trigger at a low volume threshold.
instrument: NDPC Guidance Notice on Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors of Major Importance (NDPC/HQ/GN/VOL.03/B/24)
prevents: Assuming data-protection obligations are only for big companies. A small clinic or school can qualify.
caveat: Thresholds and fee categories are set by guidance and can change. Re-check the Commission's current notice before telling any business it must or must not register.
detail: The Commission designates a controller or processor of major importance where it keeps a filing system and "processes the personal data of more than Two-Hundred (200) data subjects in six (6) months", or operates in listed sectors including financial, health, hospitality, e-commerce and education — with fees by category (N250,000 at the top level).

statement: Meta ad copy must not assert or imply a person's private attributes.
instrument: Meta Advertising Standards — Privacy Violations and Personal Attributes
prevents: "Struggling to get customers?" / "Tired of debt?" style targeting that names the reader's situation as if the advertiser knows it.
caveat: This governs ads. Organic posts are held to the Community Standards, which are related but not identical. Do not describe this as a rule for all organic copy.
detail: Ads "must not contain content that asserts or implies personal attributes", including race, religion, health, "vulnerable financial status", age, disability and criminal record; guidance shows "Do you have diabetes?" and "Are you bankrupt?" as prohibited, while "you/your" without an attribute is fine.

statement: Music in commercial or brand content on Meta needs a licence you hold.
instrument: Meta Music Guidelines (effective 26 March 2024)
prevents: Adding a trending song to a business Reel and calling it "free to use because it is in the app".
detail: "Use of music for commercial or non-personal purposes in particular is prohibited unless you have obtained appropriate licenses." Content with someone else's music "may be blocked, muted or removed"; guidance favours shorter clips, lower music density, and always a visual component.

statement: Ad review is automated first, usually inside 24 hours, and ads can be re-reviewed at any time.
instrument: Meta Advertising Standards
prevents: Treating an ad approval as permanent, or assuming Meta checks local law for you.
detail: Review "relies primarily on automated tools" and "is typically completed within 24 hours"; ads "remain subject to review and re-review" and may be rejected later; advertisers must also comply with local laws and, where applicable, self-regulatory advertising codes.

statement: WhatsApp business messaging requires opt-in, and free-form replies only inside a 24-hour window.
instrument: WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy
prevents: Importing a phone book into a broadcast tool, or auto-replying with no way to reach a person.
detail: You may only contact people who gave their number and opted in; business-initiated messages must use an approved template; you may reply without a template "within the 24-hour customer service window"; and automated replies need "prompt, clear, and direct escalation paths".

statement: TikTok separates personal-use sounds from a pre-cleared commercial library, scoped to TikTok.
instrument: TikTok Commercial Music Library terms, as summarised in music-licensing commentary
prevents: Assuming a sound cleared on TikTok is cleared for the same video on Reels or the client's website.
caveat: TikTok's own terms were not retrieved for this register (blocked on 2026-11-10). Confirm in TikTok's current Music Terms before relying on any placement claim.
detail: Business accounts are directed to the Commercial Music Library; commercial-use rights are described as covering TikTok placements only, with per-track "usable placements" listed, so cross-posting needs separate clearance.

statement: LinkedIn Page scheduling needs a Page admin role and has format limits.
instrument: LinkedIn Help — scheduled posts for Pages, as summarised in practitioner guides
prevents: Promising a client a queued carousel when the format or the role does not support it.
caveat: LinkedIn Help would not load on 2026-11-10. Confirm the role and format limits in the actual account before promising any timetable.
detail: Reported: a super admin or content admin can schedule Page posts from one hour to three months ahead; events, polls, reshares, multiple-photo posts and service posts cannot be scheduled natively.

statement: Brand typefaces are licensed for commercial use under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
instrument: SIL Open Font License 1.1 (Fraunces, Inter, JetBrains Mono)
prevents: Treating the font question as unresolved when it is in fact resolved by an open licence.
caveat: OFL covers the typefaces, not the logo, photography or any Canva Sans reference elsewhere. Those remain separate.
detail: Fraunces, Inter and JetBrains Mono are published under SIL OFL 1.1, which permits commercial use, embedding and redistribution in exported graphics. The rendered assets use fixed-weight TTF instances converted from the fontsource distribution.

statement: The site sells nine packs at a single published price of ₦5,000 each, delivered over WhatsApp.
instrument: client/src/data/offers.ts, client/src/pages/Offers.tsx
prevents: Quoting a price from memory or from an older brief, or implying the ₦297,500 figure was ever charged.
caveat: The site data is the source of the figure, not a legal review of the offer terms. If the price changes on the site, this register row is out of date until `offers_data.py` is re-run.
detail: `client/src/data/offers.ts` exports OFFER_PRICE = 5000 and nine offers, each with a keyword. Every buy button reads "Message {KEYWORD} on WhatsApp" and the contact number is +234 905 069 0837. There is no online checkout and nothing is downloadable from the site; files are sent on WhatsApp after payment is confirmed. `TOTAL_VALUE` (₦297,500) is declared in the file header as an estimate of replacement cost (hours x RATE), explicitly "not previous selling prices".

statement: Custom service work is deliberately unpriced on the site: it is quoted per brief, not sold as a pack.
instrument: client/src/data/offers.ts, client/src/pages/Offers.tsx
prevents: Advertising a ₦5,000 pack as though it included custom build work, which the FAQ rules out.
caveat: A quote for custom work must not be published as a fixed price until the owner sets one.
detail: The offer FAQ states the ₦5,000 packs include no consultation, and that custom systems or websites are "a separate paid project" priced "for a range" on WhatsApp. The service pages list categories with no published figure. A pack is a fixed-price file set; a service is a scoped quote.

statement: ₦5,000 sits inside or below the published market range for comparable Nigerian digital guides and template packs.
instrument: Digital Products for African Creators: From Idea to First Sale (Kobocourse, 2026)
prevents: Pricing a guide from instinct, or claiming a pack is a discount against a "market price" nobody measured.
caveat: A single commercial blog's ranges, not a statistical survey or a regulator's figure. It supports "inside a published range" and nothing stronger. It must never be used to imply a saving or a struck-through price.
detail: A 2026 pricing guide for African creators puts short guides and PDFs at ₦2,000-₦10,000, comprehensive workbooks at ₦8,000-₦25,000 and template packs of 3-10 items at ₦3,000-₦20,000. Each Easywurld pack is a guide plus three editable files, so ₦5,000 is at the low end of the template-pack band and inside the guide band.

statement: The logo and the Canva Sans reference in the older brief remain unverified; the typefaces now used are cleared.
instrument: marketing/operating-system-v2/skills/easywurld-human-intelligence-and-editorial-system/SKILL.md
prevents: Exporting carousels with a logo nobody can prove they own, or switching to Canva Sans without a licence.
detail: The repository contains the mark at client/public/brand/ with no provenance or licence record beside it. The v2 skill also references Canva Sans, a commercial face: it is not used in the rendered assets and is not covered by the OFL grant in REPO-03.

statement: The December track is generated copy, and its own checker says so.
instrument: marketing/operating-system-v2/{build_calendar.py,check.py}
prevents: Anyone re-reading a generated caption as though a person had signed it off.
detail: `build_calendar.py` states "Structural QA != human approval"; `check.py` states "Passing does not mean claims/design/approval passed G1-G4". 330 packages / 2,040 slide blocks / 0 rendered assets.
